bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, long-term oriented, and disciplined; emphasized 10x revenue goal over 10 years; transparent about inventory distortions and currency risks; cautious on short-term guidance due to volatility; focused on control over customer experience (no franchising yet); optimistic on luxury demand despite geopolitical tensions; proactive on hedging and India-specific product development
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: City of Time Gurgaon is not just a store but a luxury ecosystem with 5 brand boutiques + 2 multi-brand galleries + cigar lounge — a first-of-its-kind experiential hub in India; pre-owned growth (>30% YoY) is structurally supported by post-2017 cash ban increasing traceable watch supply; Favre Leuba rights in UAE are tied to prior Silvercity investment, creating a unique cross-border arbitrage opportunity; inventory buildup is strategic, not wasteful — 8 delayed boutiques were pre-stocked in Q4 to avoid GRAP IV delays
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Reinvestment-led: the deck describes an ongoing investment cycle management intends to continue for the long term, with no dividend, buyback or debt policy disclosed.
- Group structure spans Cognition Digital LLP (100% WOS), Ficus Trading LLC (100% WOS), Favre Leuba GMBH (100% WOS), Ethos Lifestyle Pvt. Ltd. (Subsidiary – 77.42*), Micron Watch Service Pvt. Ltd. (Subsidiary – 50.1%*), Silvercity Brands AG (Associate – 33.88%) and Pasadena Retail Pvt Ltd. (JV – 50%).
- In FY'26 the Lifestyle vertical was moved into a separate entity, Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited, so standalone reported PBT excludes Ethos Lifestyle's PBT.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Enduring partnerships with over 80 of the world's most prestigious watch brands, with a rising share of exclusively retailed brands that strengthens differentiation and pricing position
- Direct sourcing from brand owners, their Indian subsidiaries and authorised dealers, assuring authenticity, official warranty and protection from counterfeit and grey-market product
- Pan-India boutique network of 103 boutiques across 34 cities, giving national reach across metros and Tier-2 cities
- Omnichannel and data-led engagement supported by an extensive customer database and the Club Echo loyalty franchise, driving repeat purchase and informed assortment planning
- In-house after-sales ecosystem (Ethos Watch Care) with certified watchmakers and 100+ years of cumulative technician experience, servicing over 70 luxury watch brands
- Early-mover position in Certified Pre-Owned, a segment with limited organised competition and attractive economics
- Deep category expertise and a long track record of navigating market cycles in premium and luxury watch retail
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign exchange exposure on imported inventory (Swiss Franc) — The Company's significant dependence on imported inventory, predominantly denominated in Swiss Francs, exposes it to currency volatility - particularly appreciation of the Swiss Franc against the Rupee - which affects procurement costs and margins. This was not theoretical in FY 2025-26: management attributes the moderation in margins principally to a sharp appreciation of the Swiss Franc during the year. Mitigants are dynamic pricing, selective management of currency exposure, prudent monitoring of creditor positions and renegotiated supplier terms, plus the phased duty reduction under India-EFTA.
- Brand and supplier concentration — Dependence on a limited set of global luxury brands may pose a risk in the event of supply disruptions or changes in distribution arrangements - a structural feature of a multi-brand retailer whose economics rest on product allocation from a handful of maisons. The Company mitigates by diversifying its brand portfolio, strengthening long-term agreements, increasing the share of exclusively retailed brands and maintaining regular in-person and virtual engagement with brand partners to secure allocation.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty hitting discretionary spend — Global inflationary pressure, interest-rate movements and geopolitical developments may weaken consumer sentiment and discretionary spending within the luxury segment. Because the entire business is discretionary big-ticket retail, demand is cycle-sensitive; the Company leans on resilient HNI/UHNI customer segments, optimises product mix across price tiers and emphasises experiential retail to sustain demand through subdued periods.
- Real estate availability and expansion constraints — The limited availability of premium retail space, together with potential delays in approvals, may affect the Company's store-expansion plans - the direct constraint on a growth model built on boutique roll-out. Mitigants are asset-light approaches where feasible, prioritising high-potential locations, shop-in-shop formats and strategic partnerships, supported by its standing as a preferred retail partner for leading malls.
- Intensifying competition in luxury retail — The entry of new participants into the luxury retail space may give rise to pricing pressure and elevated marketing costs. The MD&A separately notes that the rapid formalisation of the Indian watch market and the entry of new brands - encouraged by the very India-EFTA duty reduction that benefits Ethos - are expected to intensify competition. Differentiation rests on brand positioning, customer experience, loyalty initiatives and exclusive product launches.
- Evolving consumer preferences and smartwatch substitution — The growing adoption of smartwatches and evolving fashion trends may influence demand for traditional luxury timepieces. The Company responds by reinforcing brand narratives centred on heritage and craftsmanship, broadening its offering across the premium and entry-luxury segments, and strengthening omnichannel engagement to appeal to younger consumers.
- Talent retention and capability building — Sustained performance depends on a skilled and experienced workforce, and attrition may affect service quality and operations - acute in a business where the sales advisor and the certified watchmaker are the product experience. The BRSR separately identifies employee engagement and talent management as a material issue. Mitigants are employee engagement, structured training, performance-linked incentives and leadership development.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy — Increasing digital integration heightens exposure to cyber threats and potential data breaches, and the BRSR flags that loss of sensitive customer information could bring legal penalties, heavy fines and erosion of customer trust - material given the Company's extensive customer database and its omnichannel/loyalty model. Mitigants are investment in cybersecurity infrastructure, regular audits, employee awareness and stringent data-protection measures.

outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: International expansion via UAE subsidiary (Ficus Trading LLC) to tap pre-owned market and aftersales; potential to retail Favre Leuba in UAE; e-commerce rollout for Rimowa; possible franchising study underway; expansion into Tier 2 cities (Dehradun, Vijayawada); potential for CARNAER-style display-and-order model for ultra-high-end watches
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Lifestyle-led expansion beyond watches into premium jewellery and high-end travel accessories, anchored by India's first RIMOWA boutique and a dedicated Messika boutique, to make exclusive global brands more accessible to Indian customers
- Continue broadening the retail footprint across metropolitan centres and emerging luxury markets, entering new cities (Jodhpur, Ranchi, Srinagar, Kanpur, Agra and Faridabad during the year) and adding format-specific boutiques including a second Haute Horology boutique in Mumbai
- Build Second Movement as a trusted, transparent, experience-led platform for India's pre-owned luxury watch market, supported by certified authenticity, lounges, evaluators, Ethos stores and service centres
- Widen and premiumise the brand roster through new partnerships (Faberge, FPM Milano, D1 Milano, Unimatic) that strengthen appeal among aspirational consumers and boost brand recall
- Retain the direct procurement model - sourcing from brand owners, their Indian subsidiaries and authorised dealers - as the basis of authenticity and customer trust
- Deepen omnichannel capability: India's first dedicated luxury watch app across iOS and Android, AI-led inventory optimisation, real-time analytics and personalised digital experiences built on intelligent digital infrastructure developed with AWS
- Operate a multi-format sales channel spanning metropolitan regions and Tier I, Tier II and Tier III cities through Ethos Summit Stores, multi-brand boutiques, exclusive brand outlets and Second Movement lounges
- Data-driven digital marketing and content platforms to enhance brand visibility and deepen consumer connections, supported by specialised after-sales capabilities and expert-led guidance
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Ethos is an asset-light luxury retailer, so its expansion is boutique roll-out rather than plant capex, and FY 2025-26 was described by management as the year it 'turned intent into capacity'. The Company opened 21 new stores during the year, taking the boutique count from 73 across 26 cities to 94 across 30 cities, and has since grown to 103 boutiques across 34 cities as on the date of the report, crossing the milestone of 100 boutiques by May 2026. Eight new markets were entered - Ranchi, Jodhpur, Srinagar, Kanpur, Agra, Faridabad, Visakhapatnam and Amritsar - with format additions including a second Haute Horology boutique and exclusive brand boutiques. Expansion also went vertical: the lifestyle business (Messika fine jewellery and RIMOWA luxury luggage) was carved out under a separate entity, a wholly owned subsidiary Ficus Trading LLC was incorporated with initial paid-up capital of Rs 69,87,000, and a subsidiary Micron Watch Services Private Limited was incorporated with Rs 5,01,000 of initial paid-up capital to build dedicated watch service centres. The accelerated boutique expansion carried front-loaded costs, and a rights issue completed during the year (KFin Technologies as Registrar, CRISIL as Monitoring Agency) recapitalised the balance sheet and, in management's words, gave the financial capacity to keep investing with conviction. No rupee capital-expenditure quantum is disclosed: the capital-commitments note appears in the report but carries no figure in the material supplied, and no installed-capacity table exists for this business.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's real GDP growth projected at around 6.5% for FY 2026-27, supported by resilient domestic demand, continued public capital expenditure and ongoing structural reforms
- Income-tax exemption for individuals earning up to Rs 12.75 lakh, the simplified Income Tax Act 2025 from 1 April 2026, a cumulative 100 bps repo-rate cut to 5.25%, and the 8th Pay Commission are expected to release disposable income and provide further impetus to discretionary spending, supporting demand for premium and luxury goods
- The Indian watch market is estimated at USD 4.19 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 7.52 billion by 2031 at a 10.23% CAGR, with the premium segment growing at 8.53% and online retail at 9.12%, led by metropolitan and Tier-II consumers
- India-EFTA trade agreement phasing out customs duty on Swiss watches - already down from a base of 22% to 15.71% across the first two tranches, en route to full elimination by 2031 - is set to lower retail prices, broaden the premium customer base and support margin improvement
- Swiss watch exports to India rose 8.9% in 2025 after 25.2% in 2024, making India the fastest-growing major market, and close to four in five industry executives (79%) anticipate medium-to-strong growth in India
- UBS estimates India's affluent population is likely to double by 2028 to 88 million, deepening the HNI/UHNI pool that drives structural demand for premium and luxury timepieces
- A two-speed global market: around 64% of executives view the outlook for high-end watches above CHF 50,000 positively while close to 60% rate entry-level and mid-range negatively; the global luxury watch market is projected to reach around USD 61 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of approximately 4.5%
- Pre-owned is a structural growth pool: India's pre-owned luxury watch market is expanding at a CAGR of roughly 11%, and 40% of millennial and Gen Z consumers say they are likely to buy a pre-owned watch in the coming year
- Expansion into non-metro markets and deeper retail penetration, plus e-commerce and digital discovery carrying luxury brands into Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities, are expected to drive additional growth
- Headwind: the rapid formalisation of the market and the entry of new brands are expected to intensify competition; a record-high Swiss franc and gold price lift procurement and retail costs
